newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yamaha to build Indonesian parts plant.
newsitem.headline: Yamaha to build Indonesian parts plant.

text.p: Yamaha Motor Co Ltd said on Tuesday it has formed a joint venture in Indonesia to produce motorcycle engine components.

The new company, owned 95 percent by Yamaha Motor, and five percent by an Indonesian investment company P.T. Karta Sakti Utama Motor, started building a new factory in Krawang Industrial Park, 47 kilometres east of Jakarta.
The plant will start production in October 1997 with an output capacity of 200,000 motorcycle cylinder heads and 500,000 cylinder bodies a year.
The new plant will create 200 jobs initially. The jobs at the plant are likely to increase in the future, a Yamaha spokesman said.
The products will be supplied mainly to P.T. Yamaha Indonesia Motor Manufacturing, in Pulo Gadung, suburb of Jakarta, which produces some 360,000 motorcycles per year.
The new company will begin exporting such components in 1998 to Yamaha's motorcycle output units in Asia such as its Malaysian unit and Thailand unit, the Yamaha spokesman said.
Total investment by the new company will be $23 million, the spokesman added.
